To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the transient resistance of a Luttinger wire is the sum of the Sharvin and Sharvin-like resistances of the two contacts, and (ii) the Sharvin-like resistance of a LLL is half the intrinsic resistance.

the Sharvin resistance of Luttingers liquids is half of the resistance quantum, and that a perfect junction is characterized by a total resistance of half the resistance quantum in series with half of the resistance of a semi-infinite Luttinger wire.
the contact resistance of a Luttinger/Fermliquid is half the quantum of resistance in series with the intrinsic resistance of the Luttinger liquid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of transport in low dimensional quantum systems.
the physics of interacting one-dimensional electron systems.
the transport properties of quantum wires and quantum dots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a Luttinger wire is a Fermi liquid when attached to Fermi liquid leads.
, in the presence of the electrodes, the transient and stationary conductances are identical and the contact resistance is half the intrinsic resistance, as expected for a Fermi liquid.
the contact resistance between two Luttinger liquids is the sum of the contact resistances between a Luttinger and a Fermi liquid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the contact resistance of Luttingering liquids is not universal.
the contact resistance between two interacting wires can be calculated from the intrinsic resistance of a wire in the presence of an ideal contact.
the Sharvin resistance of a Luttinger/Femi liquid is given by the sum of half the intrinsic resistance and half the quantum of resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transient conductance is a very useful tool for extracting the intrinsic resistance of a one-dimensional system.
the transient and stationary conductance of a Luttinger/Ferml liquid is not renormalized by interactions.
the Sharvin resistance of a Luttinger wire is universal and independent of the details of the junction.
